RECENT MONETARY AND FINANCIAL DEVELOPMENTS Haile Selassie Avenue P.O. Box 60000 - 00200 Nairobi \Tel: 20-2860000/2861000/ 2863000\Email: [CBK press email] CBKKenya Central Bank of Kenya www.centralbank.go.ke October 23, 2026 Economic Growth Kenya’s economy grew by 5.1 percent in the second quarter of 2026 compared to 4.9 percent in the same quarter of 2025. Growth in the quarter was supported by improved performance in transport and storage, accommodation and food services, information and communication, finance and insurance, electricity and water supply and manufacturing. The services sector continued to support economic activities and grew by 5.8 percent in 2026Q2 from 5.5 percent in 2025Q2. However, agriculture and industry sectors slowed down to 3.5 percent and 4.4 percent in 2026Q2, compared to a growth of 4.0 percent and 4.6 percent in 2025Q2, respectively (Table 1). Exchange Rates The Kenya Shilling remained stable against major international and regional currencies during the week ending October 22, 2026. It exchanged at KSh 129.91 per U.S. dollar on October 22, compared to KSh 129.81 per U.S. dollar on October 15 (Table 2). Foreign Exchange Reserves The foreign exchange reserves remained adequate at USD 14,693 million (5.9 months of import cover) as of October 22. This meets CBK’s statutory requirement to endeavour to maintain at least 4 months of import cover (Table 3). Money Market The money market remained liquid during the week ending October 22, 2026, and open market operations remained active. Commercial banks’ excess reserves averaged KSh 32.1 billion above the 3.25 percent Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) requirement. The Kenya Shilling Overnight Interbank Average (KESONIA) remained stable at 8.75 percent. During the week, the average number of interbank transactions increased to 29 from 28 in the previous week, while the average value traded increased to KSh 19.8 billion from KSh 14.9 billion in the previous week (Table 4). Government Securities Market The Treasury bill auction of October 22, received bids totalling KSh 28.8 billion against an advertised amount of KSh 28.0 billion, representing a performance of 103.0 percent. Interest rates on the 91-day, 182-day and 364-day Treasury bills declined (Table 5). Equity Market At the Nairobi Securities Exchange, the NASI, NSE 25 and NSE 20 share price indices decreased by 4.56 percent, 0.51 percent and 0.39 percent, respectively, during the week ending October 22. Market capitalization decreased by 0.38 percent while total shares traded and equity turnover increased by 6156.13 percent and 1420.48 percent respectively. The high changes in shares traded and equity turnover is attributted to a block trade of KPLC shares worth 4.5 billion shares amounting to KSh 42.5 billion (Table 7). Bond Market Bond turnover in the domestic secondary market decreased by 28.36 percent during the week ending October 22 (Table 7). In the international market, yields on Kenya’s Eurobonds increased by 2.17 basis points on average. Yields for Côte d’Ivoire and Angola also increased (Chart 2). Global Trends Inflation concerns remained during the week ending October 22. The U.K. headline inflation rose to 3.5 percent in September 2026 from 3.1 percent in August, driven mainly by higher fuel prices. The U.S. Dollar Index weakened by 0.44 percent during the week. Murban crude oil prices rose to USD 108.23 per barrel on October 22, up from USD 102.39 per barrel on October 15, reflecting elevated geopolitical risks in the Middle East and Europe.
